newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar trades tight range, awaits Friday's CPI.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar trades tight range, awaits Friday's CPI.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed little changed after trading a tight range on Wednesday but retained a soft tone in the run up to Friday's December quarter inflation data.
The currency closed at US$0.7025/32 and 68.00 on its Trade-Weighted Index, from 0.7021/28 and 67.88 at the open.
"The market's a little bit negative on the Kiwi, predominantly as a result of people's expectations for the upcoming CPI," a chief dealer said.

He said there seemed to be a groundswell of opinion that the risk for the CPI was on the low side, which could trigger either an official Reserve Bank easing or a market-led fall in rates that would take the Kiwi lower.
But he said he was personally not convinced that the time was ripe for lower rates, or that this was the start of a larger move down in the currency.
The Reserve Bank's latest forecasts were for 0.5 percent quarterly and 2.3 percent annual underlying inflation, but economists expect 0.4 percent and 2.15 percent respectively.
The chief dealer said the currency could rise if inflation came in at or above expectations.
The Australian dollar again lost ground, but it had little impact on the Kiwi, which was supported by some corporate buying and option-related interest.
An Auckland dealer predicted a 0.7015-45 overnight range.
